they who sustain all things upon the earth, devouring like a calf its mother cow.
Bring forth the god Jātavedas with divine prayer;
may he carry our oblations to him in due order.
And this very one, seeking the gods, is led forth as the Hotṛ for the sacrifice; like a well-guarded chariot, he, glowing with heat, takes heed by himself.
This Agni protects us as if from an immortal birth;
he, the god more powerful than power itself, has been established for the sake of life.
The wise behold with their heart and mind the Bird anointed by the magic power of the Asura;
within the ocean, the seers discern him; the ordainers seek his station among the rays of light.
The bird bears speech within his mind; the Gandharva uttered it within the womb. At the station of Eternal Order (ṛta), the seers guard that shining, celestial wisdom.
I have seen the Herdsman, who never rests, moving hither and thither along his paths;
clothed in converging and diverging rays, he revolves repeatedly within the worlds.
Hither let us invoke for our well-being that swift Tārkṣya, the prize-winner urged by the gods, the victorious overcomer of chariots, whose rim is uninjured, who conquers in battle.
Invoking the bounty of Indra as it were, may we embark upon you for our well-being as if upon a ship.
O wide, broad, vast, and deep ones, may we not be harmed by these two of yours when they come near nor when they have passed away.
He who by his might has instantly overspread the five peoples, as the sun with its light overspreads the waters—
he whose speed wins thousands and hundreds, no one can restrain him, any more than a young woman can hold back a flying arrow.
Arise, look upon Indra’s seasonal portion!
If it is cooked, offer it; if it is not yet cooked, wait for me.
The oblation is cooked; come hither, O Indra! The sun has reached the middle of its path.
Your friends sit around you with their offerings, like householders surrounding the lord of a caravan as he travels.
I consider it cooked in the udder, cooked on the fire; I consider this newest *ṛta* to be well-cooked.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, doer of many deeds, drink of the curd from the midday libation with pleasure.
O much-invoked one, you have utterly subdued your enemies; let your might be supreme and your bounty be here.
O Indra, bring us riches with your right hand; you are the lord of the wealthy rivers.
Like a fearsome beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, you have come hither from the furthest distance.
Having sharpened your bolt and your keen blade, O Indra, strike down our enemies and drive away those who oppose us.
O Indra, you were born for the sake of desirable dominion and power, O bull among the peoples.
You drove away the unfriendly folk and made wide space for the gods.
From Dhātṛ, Dyutāna, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu, Vasiṣṭha brought forth the *rathantara* [sāman], which is the oblation of the oblation belonging to the *anuṣṭubh* whose names are Pratha and Sapratha.
They found that which was hidden away, the supreme station of the sacrifice that lay in the secret cave;
from the radiant Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu, Bharadvāja brought forth the lofty [song] of Agni.
Meditating with their minds, they found the first *yajuḥ*, the path traveled by the gods;
from Dhātṛ, Dyutāna, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu, from Sūrya, these [sages] brought forth the *gharma*.

May Bṛhaspati lead us across difficult passages; may he turn back the malevolent thought of the one who speaks evil. May he cast away the curse and strike down the ill-intentioned; then may he grant well-being and peace to the sacrificer.
May Narāśaṃsa protect us at the fore-offering; may there be well-being for us at the after-offering during our invocations.
May he swiftly strike down the curse and drive away evil intent, and then grant the sacrificer peace and prosperity.
May he whose head is glowing heat burn up the demons who hate the sacred word, so that they may be slain by his arrow.
May he swiftly strike away the curse and the evil thought, and then bring peace and well-being to the sacrificer.
I beheld you with my mind, you who are conscious, born of heat, manifested from heat.
Bestowing upon us offspring here and wealth here, be procreated through progeny, O you who desire a son!
I beheld you with my mind as you were meditating, crying out in your own body for the sake of the season.
O young woman, rise up toward me; beget offspring through progeny, O you who desire a son!
I have placed the germ within the plants; I am within all existing beings. I have generated offspring upon the earth; I have brought forth sons from their mothers hereafter.
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms;
may Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you.
Bestow the embryo, O Sinīvālī; bestow the embryo, O Sarasvatī.
May the two divine Aśvins, wreathed with lotuses, place the embryo within you.
O Aśvins, that which you churn forth from the two golden fire-sticks—
him we invoke as your embryo, to be born in the tenth month.
Great shall be the celestial protection of the three— of Mitra, Aryaman,
and Varuṇa— which is invincible.
Neither at home nor on the obstructed paths is the evil-plotting enemy master over them.
To that mortal man for whom the sons of Aditi grant imperishable light so that he may live, [to him they give it].
May Vāta breathe forth healing for us, bringing bliss and joy to our heart;
may he prolong our lives.
O Vāta, you are our father, and you are our brother and our friend;
as such, grant us life to live.
O Vāta, that treasure of immortality which is placed in your house yonder— grant us from it so that we may live.
Send forth your speech toward Agni, the bull of the peoples;
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who shines forth from the farthest distance, across the desert wastes—
he shall carry us safely beyond our enemies.
He who, as a bull with his bright flame, utterly consumes the demons—
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who looks out upon all beings and beholds them together— may he carry us across our enemies.
That bright Agni who was born on the far shore of this realm—
he shall carry us across our enemies.
Now, indeed, urge forth Jātavedas, the spirited horse,
so that he may sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
I offer a great hymn of praise to this Jātavedas, the bounteous one, whose heroes are inspired sages.
Those radiances of Jātavedas which carry the oblations to the gods—
by means of them, may he further our sacrifice.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled before his mother, and advancing toward heaven, he has approached his father.
Moving within the luminous spheres, breathing out from his breath,
the Great One has revealed the sky.
He shines across thirty stations; speech is bestowed upon the winged bird, day after day, throughout the mornings.
From the heat of the kindled ascetic fervor (tapas), Ṛta and Satya were born;
from that, night was born, and from that, the billowing ocean.
From the ocean, the billowing sea, the year was born;
ordaining days and nights, the Lord over all that blinks.
The Ordainer fashioned the sun and the moon as they were before;
he fashioned heaven and earth, the intermediate space, and likewise the sky.
O bull-like Agni, you gather together all the riches of the noble one;
kindled at the place of libation, bring us treasures here.
Come together, speak together; let your minds be in accord, just as the gods of old, being in harmony, attend to their portion.
Common is the counsel, common the assembly, common the mind, and their thought is united. I address you with a common prayer; I offer to you with a common oblation.
United be your intention, united be your hearts;
let your mind be one, so that you may act in harmony together.
